placements.why: All five segments concern a technical deployment gate for the Meridian release train — a signed-manifest requirement, its scope across staging and production, the incident that prompted it, and who owns it. This is release/deployment engineering content, and the supplied strata is empty — nothing exists to hold it. Minting Architecture as a standing top-level category gives this and future release-engineering content (Meridian or otherwise) a home, matching the org's named taxonomy space rather than inventing an unrelated bucket.
placements.title: Release and deployment engineering decisions get their own standing organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content concern how software is built, verified, and shipped through technical pipelines, as distinct from market strategy, product scope, or organizational process design?

placements.title: Deploys must clear a cryptographic verification gate before shipping, not just a process sign-off
placements.frame: Is a deployment being conditioned on a verified release manifest as a hard precondition, and what scope, exceptions, ownership, or triggering incidents does that gate accrue as it recurs?
placements.why: src-1 and src-3 state the identical requirement — a signed release manifest gates every Meridian deploy — once in directive prose and once as a compressed spec line; src-4 extends that gate's jurisdiction to staging and production; src-5 assigns ownership to Quinton Fairweather; src-2 supplies the concrete incident (two unsigned artifacts reaching staging last quarter) that evidences why the gate exists, per the rule that a one-time fact joins the supporting segments of the theme it motivates rather than minting its own leaf. Together these name a standing release-verification control — not a single fact — that future envelopes about this or other release trains will keep feeding as the gate is enforced, rescoped, or exempted. Nothing in the (empty) existing graph structure covers deployment/release verification, so this is a genuine mint, placed under the newly-minted Architecture strata rather than left parentless.
